subject: Post-demo: performance checkpoints and geo-routing / residency commitments
messages:
From: Rachel Kim <rachel.kim@redwood.com>
To: Liam O'Connor <liam.oconnor@holohealth.com>, Aria Singh <aria.singh@holohealth.com>
Cc: Sean Gallagher <sean.gallagher@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 03 Aug 2026 15:10:00 -0700
Subject: Post-demo: performance checkpoints and geo-routing / residency commitments

Hi Liam / Aria —

Great to meet today — thanks for walking us through the candidate flows and peak traffic estimates. Quick recap and a handful of asks so we can scope the pilot and outstanding compliance checks:

Key targets you mentioned (please confirm if these are final):
- P95 latency target: 120 ms for short generation paths (prompt + <256 tokens) in US and EU.
- APAC tolerance: up to 250 ms p95 for the first phase; long-term goal is <=150 ms.
- Sustained throughput: 500 requests per minute with typical concurrency of 40–60 concurrent streams.
- Streaming: token streaming at 5–8 tokens/sec per stream (real-time product).

Data residency constraints:
- EU customer data must remain and be processed within EU regions (no cross-border caching).
- APAC production must not persist logs outside APAC for regulated patient flows; storing aggregated telemetry in central analytics is OK if anonymized.

Immediate asks / next steps:
1) Please share a short sample network trace (eg outbound ports, RTT from your app gateways to us-east/us-west/eu-west apis) — that will let us validate routing and TCP handshake times.
2) Confirm the procurement contact and preferred timeline for contractual review (Aria?) so we can prepare the Dedicated capacity and data residency addendum.
3) Accept/modify the preliminary SLO matrix I attached (slo_matrix_v1.xlsx). We propose a pilot SLO at p95=150ms in APAC and 120ms US/EU with auto-fallback to a lower-cost model for >95th percentile spikes.

I'll loop Sean and Ben for technical qualification and to propose an ops runbook for the pilot. Proposed follow-up: 30-min SE deep-dive on Wed 8/5 afternoon PT — does that work?

Thanks,
Rachel

Redwood Inference

Subject: Re: Post-demo: performance checkpoints and geo-routing / residency commitments

Thanks Rachel — nice summary. A couple quick clarifications from our side:

- P95 targets look good for US/EU. For APAC, the 250ms cap is conservative — apologies, that's what our product team suggested to be safe. If you think 150ms pilot is achievable by routing, happy to test.
- Throughput: 500 rpm is our upper bound during peak marketing events; typical is 200–300 rpm. Concurrency spikes to ~120 during special campaigns for <15 minutes.
- Streaming token rate: 7 tokens/sec is accurate for the patient dialog stream.

Residency: Aria — procurement and legal are on standby but need a short description of the technical controls that guarantee EU-only processing (network egress, KV cache placement, logging retention). Also, for APAC we need an option where logs and full request payloads are never exported out of Singapore.

I'll attach our sample app-level trace shortly (will send as a separate email). For the SE call, Wed 8/5 3pm PT works for me.

—Liam
Liam O'Connor | Head of Platform Engineering
HoloHealth
liam.oconnor@holohealth.com
From: Sean Gallagher <sean.gallagher@redwood.com>
To: Rachel Kim <rachel.kim@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 04 Aug 2026 09:05:00 -0700
Subject: Fwd: Post-demo: performance checkpoints and geo-routing / residency commitments

Rachel / Ben — forwarding Liam's note and adding a few technical constraints and proposed pilot configuration.

On the routing/residency side:
- We can map tenant traffic by region using edge routing + regional model placement. For EU-only processing we will pin model inference shards and KV cache to eu-west-1 and ensure no cross-region KV cache warming.
- For APAC data residency, we offer two options: (A) Singapore region with strict logging retention + HSM-based key wrap (meets most needs), or (B) Private deployment (VPC) in your data center for fully air-gapped processing (longer lead time).

Performance configuration for the pilot (recommended):
- US/EU: model variant A (8-bit quantized) on shared-hosted for cost-effective throughput; target p95 <= 120ms.
- APAC: dedicated burst pool (reserved instances) with model variant B (FP16) to reduce jitter; target p95 <= 150ms for the pilot.
- Concurrency/throughput: We'll provision for baseline 60 concurrent but will autoscale to 200 for 15-minute campaign windows. Continuous batching will reduce per-token CPU but can add ~10–20 ms to p95—documented in the SLO sheet.

Requests from our side to validate:
1) Sample network traces (Liam said he'll send).
2) A representative request/response size distribution (average token length per request, average response tokens).
3) Legal confirmation on the list of EU accounts that require strict in-region processing.

I'll attach a short ops checklist and the sample network trace we use in-house. Ben — once you review the SLO spreadsheet please add any quantization/recommendation rows (I left a placeholder for 4-bit vs 8-bit).

Thanks,
Sean
Sean Gallagher | Solutions Architect, Redwood Inference
sean.gallagher@redwood.com

Liam / Aria / Procurement —

Thanks — appreciate the quick responses. Confirming agreed items and a tight set of next steps so procurement has visibility:

Agreed (preliminary):
- Pilot SLOs: US/EU p95 <= 120ms; APAC pilot p95 <= 150ms.
- Pilot capacity: baseline 60 concurrent, autoscale to 200 for short bursts; target sustained 500 rpm for full pilot.
- Data residency: EU processing pinned to eu-west-1; APAC logs retained in APAC by default.

Action items and owners:
- Liam: Send sample network traces + representative payload sizes (ASAP).
- Aria / Procurement: Share procurement contact and any redline templates by Fri 8/6.
- Sean / Ben: Finalize SLO matrix (attached) with quantization recommendations and expected cost delta for dedicated APAC pool.
- Rachel: Schedule SE deep-dive Wed 8/5 3pm PT (calendar invite sent).

I've attached the SLO matrix (slo_matrix_v1.xlsx) and the draft dedicated proposal. Link to the HubSpot deal with notes: https://app.hubspot.com/contacts/12345/deal/HL-4721

Thanks all — talk Wed.
